definition: Lexical choice is the subtask of Natural language generation that involves choosing the content words (nouns, non-auxiliary verbs, adjectives, and adverbs) in a generated text.
details: Function words (determiners, for example) are usually chosen during realisation.
story: Think of a jazz musician who has heard so many solos that a new one simply falls out of their fingers. Given a starting line, the machine imagines what comes next — a word, a note, a patch of a picture. It makes new things by recombining everything it has ever seen. Creation, here, is memory recombined at speed. And that is Lexical choice — making something new out of everything it has ever seen.
